params.body:
Eight sites carry a `exposure:csp` task, and for a person that task is a blank page: a content security policy says which scripts may run, and nobody knows that from outside. What **is** measurable is what the page loads today, and this scan already saw it while parsing the page. It threw that away and kept a count.

It now publishes the sources the way a policy is written:

- `sources`: per third-party host the kinds it is referenced as (`script`, `style`, `image`, `frame`), sorted; the own host left out because `'self'` covers it, and a host that appears only inside script code left out because nobody can see from outside whether it is ever fetched.
- `inlineScripts` and `inlineStyles`: what no host list can cover. A policy without `'unsafe-inline'` breaks exactly those, so whoever writes one has to know they are there first.

No hand and no judgement: this is the evidence a person writes a policy from. A hand can follow once this list has proven itself on a few sites — that order is the point, after a day in which two mechanisms were proposed before anyone had checked they could work.

662 tests, PHPStan, Pint.
params.title: Wat een pagina laadt, en waarvandaan
